newsitem.title: UK: Shell says seventh Nigerian oil plant occupied.
newsitem.headline: Shell says seventh Nigerian oil plant occupied.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell said on Thursday a seventh oil installation on the Niger Delta was occupied last Saturday by local villagers, forcing the oil giant to cut back production by a total of 210,000 barrels per day (bpd).
"Shell was given 12 hours notice to stop operations and evacuate all staff from the Nembe Creek flow station," said a company spokesman in London.

Nembe Creek, in the eastern Niger Delta, was occupied on Saturday along with six Shell installations in the western delta by local tribesmen protesting the relocation of their local government headquarters.
Nigerian villagers released a further 35 Shell staff held in the western region on Thursday and agreed to free the rest later in the day. No Shell workers were being held at Nembe Creek.
But Shell said it was too early to say when operations could resume and confirmed it had issued a precautionary warning of force majeure on some exports from April 2.

"We are hoping to resume production as soon as possible but the first step is to ensure that the occupations of the flow stations has ceased and that it is safe for our people to return," said the spokesman.
